newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish customs staff plan go-slow from Sunday.
newsitem.headline: Polish customs staff plan go-slow from Sunday.

text.p: Unions grouping about 40 percent of Poland's customs officers plan to start a go-slow protest next week which could cause long queues at border crossings and cargo airports, their leader said on Friday.
Union leader Andrzej Gajda told Reuters the protest was likely to be held for four hours on Sunday, starting at midday, and then bite full-time from Monday.
It would involve careful checks of 50 percent of the goods crossing Poland's borders, instead of the current 10 percent or less, and meticulous inspection of documentation.

"This means that we will check at least every other car, every other parcel," said Gajda, head of the Federation of Trade Unions of Customs Administration Employees, which includes about 5,000 officers.
"Queues are going to get longer," he added.
Air cargo industry sources said the action, known in Poland as an "Italian strike", could cause serious delays.
Gajda said customs staff now received about half their pay in the form of bonuses which did not come from the state budget and were not legally guaranteed.
He said they sought contractual assurances for this element of their pay until a proposed new law on the customs service, which would contain such provisions, passed through parliament.

Main Customs Office (GUC) spokeswoman Elzbieta Drabarek said the administration's chief hoped for an understanding with the unions but he had little influence over the budget, which had in any case been set for 1997 and had increased bonuses.
"It would be hard for us to make any promises that would require a change in the budget," she said.

"We hope the form of protest that has been announced will not be implemented and this scenario will not happen," she told Reuters but she was unable to say whether there would be any talks with unions before the planned start of the protest. -- Anthony Barker +48 22 653 9700
